# ome-client-rs

Rust client for the OME (`ome.io/v1beta1`) CRDs — the Rust analog of `pkg/client`,
a peer of it (lives at the repo top level, reusable beyond MUSE).

## Layout

- `src/<crd>.rs` — kube-native types generated by [`kopium`](https://github.com/kube-rs/kopium)
  from `config/crd/full/ome.io_*.yaml` (the same CRDs `make manifests` produces).
  **Generated — do not edit by hand; run `make rust-client`.** (~86k lines; the
  ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime modules are large because the pod-template
  schema is inlined.)
- `src/client.rs` — `OmeClient`, a clientset-style handle (typed `kube::Api<T>`
  per kind). Feature `client`.
- `src/informers.rs` — `SharedInformerFactory`, `shared_informer`, and `Informer`
  (a watcher+reflector keeping a `Store`, with event `subscribe()`). Feature `runtime`.
- `src/listers.rs` — `Lister<K>` over the informer cache: get / list / namespaced
  + equality and set-based `LabelSelector` filters. Feature `runtime`.

The clientset/informer/lister layer is hand-written (~500 lines) over kube-rs
generics — there is no client-go-style code generator for it in Rust.

## Regenerate

```sh
make rust-client          # kopium over ../config/crd/full/
```

## Test

```sh
make rust-integration-test   # boots etcd + kube-apiserver from the controller-runtime
                             # envtest assets (no Docker), installs the OME CRDs, and
                             # exercises clientset CRUD + informer/lister convergence
                             # + event subscription against a real apiserver.
```

> Large generated types deserialize on the reflector's thread and can overflow
> the default 2 MiB stack — run consumers with a large tokio `thread_stack_size`
> (the tests set `RUST_MIN_STACK`; the Makefile target does this for you).
